The returning tide

At low water the rock ledge is a narrow bridge. Small pools remain between the stones, each holding a few strands of weed and a patch of sand. Across the channel, a heron waits beside the reeds.

The first ripple reaches the marker before the rest of the channel begins to fill. The water creeps around the stones and joins the pools one after another. We note the time against the height of the ledge.

By the next observation the sand has disappeared. The narrow bridge has become an island. A second mark on the ruler shows how far the tide has risen since the first ripple crossed the channel.
